aliases: Brazilian black bean and pork stew

winner.title: Feijoada
winner.source: NYT Cooking (Francis Lam, Michelli Guimaraes Knauer)

evidence.authenticity: Traditional pig parts (feet, tails, tongue), slab bacon, smoked sausage, black beans, onion-garlic refogado stirred in at the end; co-credited to Brazilian cook Michelli Guimaraes Knauer; headnote says flavor should be beany and porky, not smoky; serves with rice, orange, farofa and Brazilian collards (both linked as separate recipes on the page).
evidence.precision: Weights for the meats and beans (only 2 of 15 lines have lb weights in the signal count, but meats are sized in lb and cut sizes are given); 8 sensory cues across 3 steps (skim foam for 40 min, tender but not falling apart, stew rich but not stiff, onion evenly browned, garlic golden, oil shimmering); no pan size beyond 'heavy pot'; water depth given (cover by 1 inch, about 10 cups, keep covered by 1/2 inch).
evidence.testing: NYT Cooking editorial test process; 241 ratings averaging 4.0; headnote explains why feet and tails (gelatin, piggy flavor) and warns against too much smoke; step explains that breaking up some beans makes the stew creamy.
evidence.photos: Process photos are not visible to read; 46 images on page but structured data has none for steps. Scored conservatively.
evidence.efficiency: 3.5 hrs total, no soak (unsoaked beans), onion cooked in parallel while the stew finishes.
evidence.access: Pigs' feet, tails and tongue need a butcher or Latin/Asian market; headnote offers more sausage, fresh pork belly or other cuts as substitutes. Andouille or kielbasa as the sausage.

winner.why: It has the most authentic meat mix with Brazilian co-authorship, the clearest doneness cues, and no overnight soak, while the runner-up is a longer-ingredient-list version with fewer cues and harder-to-find items.

runnerUp.title: Feijoada

evidence.authenticity: Brazilian author; paio, calabresa, carne seca, smoked ribs; desalting steps, serves with farofa, collards, vinagrete, torresmo.
evidence.precision: Gram weights on 8 of 17 ingredient lines; few cues (browned, foam skimming); no pan size; pressure-cooker only.
evidence.testing: Little explanation of why; single rating.
evidence.photos: 29 images on page, step photos not confirmed.
evidence.efficiency: About 100 min using a pressure cooker.
evidence.access: Paio, calabresa and carne seca are hard to find in the US with no substitutes listed.

runnerUp.why: Authentic and precise on weights, but it needs a pressure cooker and Brazilian specialty meats with no substitutions.

notes: NYT page links to separate farofa and Brazilian collard greens recipes, but their URLs were not read this run so no companions are recorded. Serious Eats article page (feijoada-brazilian-stew-pork-beans) has no structured data and was not read with WebFetch; the Hardcore Feijoada recipe was scored instead and is a 6 to 8 hour simmer with an overnight soak. Woks of Life, BBC and A Spicy Perspective are Westernized or use substituted meats (ham hock, Buddig, Mexican chorizo, tomatoes). Scores for Woks of Life, BBC and A Spicy Perspective are rough estimates, not itemized.
